description: User configures an MQTT user account managed by pgmqttd. controller-runtime's K8s Lease elects exactly one reconciler at a time across Pods; the elected Pod materialises each User into a row in the broker's Postgres `users` table.

spec.description: UserSpec defines the desired state of User.

passwordSecretRef.description:
References an existing Secret holding the password. The
key must hold a non-empty value.
Omit to have the reconciler generate a credentials Secret
named `<metadata.name>-mqtt-credentials` containing
`username`, `password` and `host`, plus `port`/`uri`
for the TCP listener and `ws-port`/`ws-uri` for the
websocket listener, each only while that listener is
enabled. When the broker is given a TLS endpoint
(`PGMQTT_TLS_HOST`) the Secret also carries `tls-host`,
and `tls-port`/`mqtts-uri` and `wss-port`/`wss-uri`
for whichever of those ports is configured.

username.description:
MQTT username. Defaults to `metadata.name` when empty.
A username belongs to the first User that claims it,
in any namespace. Another User asking for the same
one gets no account and reports `UsernameConflict`
on its Ready condition until the owner is deleted or
renamed.
Restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}` so a malformed
name can't bloat broker storage or push the
pg_notify takeover/quota payloads (which carry the
username) past Postgres' 8 KB per-NOTIFY hard limit.

status.description: UserStatus defines the observed state of User.

observedSecretHash.description:
Deprecated and always empty. Releases before 0.3.0
stored a SHA-256 of the password here; the reconciler
clears it on its first pass over the User.

observedSecretVersion.description:
Identity (`<uid>/<resourceVersion>`) of the Secret the
password was last read from. While the Secret still
has it, the reconciler knows the password is unchanged
without comparing it against the stored hash.

observedUsername.description:
MQTT username most recently reconciled into the
broker's `users` table. The reconciler compares
this to the currently-derived username (spec.username
or metadata.name) and deletes the old row when they
diverge — preventing orphan rows on spec.username
rename.
